lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Agriculture Fundamentals Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What is the main aim of this course?
options: To teach digital tools applied to real farming problems
To teach farming without any technology
questions.explanation: AgriTech is the meeting point of agriculture and digital tools; the course teaches you to apply the tools to real farms.

questions.question: What are the four things every farming system manages?
questions.explanation: These four cover the physical basis of every farming system regardless of scale.

questions.question: What are the four layers of digital agriculture?
questions.explanation: Each layer feeds the next, and the chain delivers value only if all four function.

questions.question: Which rainfall change usually damages West African farming most?
options: Changes in distribution, such as a shifting onset and dry spells
A small fall in the annual total
questions.explanation: Crops respond to water available at critical stages, so distribution matters more than the annual total.

questions.question: What is usually the binding constraint on a smallholding?
options: Peak-period labour or cash at planting
questions.explanation: Land is often available while labour during peak weeks and cash at planting run out first.

questions.question: What accuracy does a typical phone GPS achieve?
questions.explanation: Phone-grade GPS is accurate to a few metres, which is sufficient for mapping plots and marking sample points.

questions.question: What are the four parts of an IoT device?
options: Solar panel, antenna, memory and clock
Sensor, processor, radio and power source
questions.explanation: Every such device must measure, format, transmit and be powered.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of a fixed-wing drone?
options: It covers much larger areas per flight
questions.explanation: Fixed-wing aircraft are far more efficient in forward flight, so they survey larger areas per battery.

lessons.title: 📝 Precision Agriculture Assessment
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Precision Agriculture Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: Where should data collection design begin?
options: With the questions you want to answer
questions.explanation: The questions determine which fields must be recorded, and missing fields cannot be recovered later.

questions.question: Why do maximum yield and maximum profit rarely coincide?
options: Because prices fall as yield rises
Because extra inputs eventually cost more than the extra output is worth
questions.explanation: Diminishing returns mean the last increments of yield cost more than they earn.

questions.question: Which platform matters most for agricultural trade in West Africa?
questions.explanation: WhatsApp is where buyers, traders and farmers already communicate and transact.

questions.question: What are the three types of food hazard?
questions.explanation: These three categories cover every way food can become unsafe.

questions.question: What does inelastic demand mean for staple food?
options: Consumption changes little when the price changes
questions.explanation: People eat roughly the same amount regardless of price, so supply changes hit price hard.

questions.question: What does AI in agriculture fundamentally do?
options: Finds patterns in data to classify or predict
Understands crops the way an agronomist does
questions.explanation: It is trained pattern-matching applied to classification and prediction tasks.

questions.question: What should you ask first about any agricultural policy?
questions.explanation: Every policy transfers value, and identifying the direction reveals its real effect.

questions.question: Where should the conclusion or request appear?
questions.explanation: A busy reader may stop early, so the essential point must come first.

lessons.title: 📝 IoT & Drone Technology Assessment
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

IoT & Drone Technology Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: Why does a portfolio matter more than a certificate?
options: It shows what you produced rather than what you were taught
questions.explanation: Evidence of completed work demonstrates capability that a course record cannot.

questions.question: What makes a tool count as AgriTech?
options: It is expensive and recently invented
questions.explanation: The test is whether the tool changes a decision, not how advanced or costly it is.

questions.question: Which two decisions usually have the largest effect on yield?
questions.explanation: Both are made before planting and set the ceiling for everything that follows.

questions.question: What is the loop at the centre of smart farming?
options: Observe, decide, act, observe the result
questions.explanation: Smart farming responds to conditions through a closing feedback loop rather than following a fixed calendar.

questions.question: What are the three objectives of climate-smart agriculture?
questions.explanation: All three must be pursued together for a practice to qualify as climate-smart.

questions.question: What question does resource management ask of every resource?
options: What is the return on the next unit of it?
questions.explanation: Comparing marginal returns is what directs each scarce resource to its best use.

questions.question: What is the central capability of a GIS?
options: Overlaying layers so questions can span several datasets
questions.explanation: Combining layers that share a coordinate system is what allows multi-factor spatial questions.

questions.question: Why is sensor drift worse than simple inaccuracy?
options: Because the error changes over time and cannot be corrected once
questions.explanation: A constant offset can be corrected; an error that changes cannot be, without recalibration.

lessons.title: 📝 Farm Management Assessment
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Farm Management Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What is an orthomosaic?
options: A single geometrically corrected image of a whole field
A three-dimensional model of a building
questions.explanation: Individual overlapping photographs are stitched and corrected into one measurable image.

questions.question: When does dedicated software beat a spreadsheet?
options: When the crop is high value
When the farm is large in area
When several people record data and reports are needed regularly
questions.explanation: Multi-user entry and repeated reporting are what a spreadsheet handles poorly.

questions.question: Why do farmers typically capture a small share of chain value?
options: Because their step has least differentiation, most competition and weakest price information
questions.explanation: Structural position rather than dishonesty explains the small share.

questions.question: What does farm branding promise, as distinct from product branding?
options: A relationship, including reliability and responsiveness
questions.explanation: Buyers of repeat supply are purchasing dependability, which attaches to the farm.

questions.question: Where do most farms fail a GAP audit?
questions.explanation: Compliance must be demonstrated through documentation, and that is usually what is missing.

questions.question: How is net farm income calculated?
options: Total gross margin minus fixed costs
questions.explanation: Gross margins cover variable costs, so fixed costs are then deducted to reach net farm income.

questions.question: What is overfitting?
options: Predicting values that are too high
A model memorising training examples and failing on new data
questions.explanation: The model captures noise specific to its training set rather than the general relationship.

questions.question: What is customary tenure?
options: A rental agreement with a bank
Land rights recognised by the community and traditional authorities
questions.explanation: It is community-recognised rights administered outside the statutory titling system.

lessons.title: 📝 Agribusiness Assessment
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Agribusiness Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What does influence rest on when formal authority is limited?
questions.explanation: Without authority, people cooperate because they trust your judgement and your word.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a resume?
questions.explanation: It is a screening document whose only job is to get you to the next stage.

questions.question: How does digital agriculture differ from AgriTech?
options: They are exactly the same thing
Digital agriculture is specifically about information and data
Digital agriculture excludes the use of phones
questions.explanation: AgriTech includes physical innovations; digital agriculture is the information-focused subset.

questions.question: What is usually the largest cost in intensive livestock production?
questions.explanation: Feed typically accounts for 60 to 70 percent of production cost in intensive systems.

questions.question: What is precision agriculture fundamentally about?
options: Reducing the number of crops grown
questions.explanation: The core idea is measuring and responding to within-field variation instead of averaging across it.

questions.question: Why is surface runoff a double loss?
options: It takes water and topsoil away
questions.explanation: Runoff removes both the water the crop needed and the fertile topsoil it carries.

questions.question: What is gross margin?
questions.explanation: Gross margin subtracts only variable costs, which allows enterprises to be compared fairly.

questions.question: What does NDVI actually indicate?
options: The exact cause of crop stress
Where vegetation differs in vigour from its surroundings
questions.explanation: It highlights differences in vegetation vigour; identifying the cause needs a field visit.

lessons.title: 📝 Data Analytics Assessment
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Data Analytics Assessment

Complete this assessment, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What two reference points give a moisture reading meaning?
questions.explanation: Usable water lies between these two points, and both depend on the soil.

questions.question: What is the economic argument for crop monitoring?
options: Early detection provides days of warning while intervention is still possible
questions.explanation: Finding a problem while it can still be fixed is where the value lies.

questions.question: What structure should farm data be held in?
options: A flat table with one row per event
questions.explanation: Flat tables are what pivot tables, filters and conditional functions require to work.

questions.question: What four questions should market research answer?
options: How much land, labour, cash and time
Who buys, what quantity and quality, when, and at what price
Where to plant, when to plant, what to plant, and how much
Which seed, which fertiliser, which market, which buyer
questions.explanation: These four determine whether a planned crop can be sold profitably.

questions.question: What is the hardest part of agricultural e-commerce?
options: Fulfilment: picking, packing, freshness and delivery
questions.explanation: Perishable goods make the logistics far harder than the selling.

questions.question: What is the dominant factor in fresh produce deterioration?
questions.explanation: Respiration accelerates with temperature, so removing field heat quickly extends shelf life.

questions.question: Which statement shows what a business owns and owes at a point in time?
questions.explanation: A balance sheet is a snapshot of assets, liabilities and the equity between them.

questions.question: What most often causes poor computer vision results in the field?
questions.explanation: Framing, focus and lighting determine whether the model receives an image it can interpret.

lessons.title: 🧪 Midterm Examination
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Midterm Examination

Complete this examination/review, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: Which SDG is the primary agricultural goal?
questions.explanation: Goal 2 covers hunger, nutrition, agricultural productivity and smallholder incomes directly.

questions.question: What is distinctive about agricultural project deadlines?
options: Many tasks are season-locked and cannot move
They are set by donors only
questions.explanation: Biological timing fixes certain dates, and everything upstream must fit before them.

questions.question: How do recruiters typically find candidates on LinkedIn?
questions.explanation: Search by skill and tool keywords is the standard method, so those words must appear.

questions.question: Which combination is hardest for employers to find?
options: Someone who can only work in the field
Someone who can do both field agronomy and data work
Someone who can only analyse data
questions.explanation: Bridge skills are scarce; most candidates are strong in one family and weak in the other.

questions.question: Why do subsistence systems value reliability over maximum yield?
options: Because a failed season means the household has no food
questions.explanation: When the harvest is the household's food supply, avoiding failure matters more than achieving a peak.

questions.question: What should every farm record attach to?
questions.explanation: Attaching records to plot and date is what makes later comparison and explanation possible.

questions.question: Why is soil loss treated as effectively permanent?
options: Because soil forms far more slowly than it erodes
questions.explanation: Formation takes centuries per centimetre while erosion can remove it in one storm.

questions.question: What four elements does a usable farm record contain?
options: What, where, when and how much
questions.explanation: Without any one of these the record cannot be linked to a plot, a time or a quantity.

questions.question: What does yield monitoring add beyond a total harvest figure?
options: It shows where within the field output varies
questions.explanation: Recording output by plot exposes within-field variation that a single total conceals.

questions.question: Why does on-farm rainfall measurement matter?
options: Rainfall is intensely local and can differ greatly over a few kilometres
questions.explanation: Convective rainfall varies sharply over short distances, so distant figures can be badly wrong.

questions.question: What do ground control points provide?
options: Anchoring of the map to true real-world positions
questions.explanation: Without surveyed references the map can be internally consistent yet offset from true position.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a dashboard?
options: To display everything that is known
To answer whether anything is wrong and the season is on track, at a glance
questions.explanation: A dashboard is for rapid situational awareness, not comprehensive reporting.

questions.question: What is the weakest competitive position?
questions.explanation: Undifferentiated commodity supply leaves price as the only lever, which is a race downwards.

questions.question: What is the real cost of selling through a marketplace?
options: Commission and control of the customer relationship
questions.explanation: Losing the direct relationship leaves the business exposed to the platform's decisions.

questions.question: What is the critical variable for safe grain storage?
questions.explanation: Above roughly 13 to 14 percent moisture, mould develops and can produce aflatoxin.

lessons.title: 🧪 Final Examination
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Final Examination

Complete this examination/review, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: How is payback period calculated?
options: Investment cost divided by additional annual net income
questions.explanation: It measures how long the additional net income takes to recover the outlay.

questions.question: What makes a prediction valuable besides accuracy?
options: Lead time, so there is opportunity to act
questions.explanation: A prediction arriving after the decision window has closed cannot change anything.

questions.question: How is environmental compliance increasingly enforced?
options: Through the market, by buyers and certification schemes
questions.explanation: Buyers audit and withdraw business, which is often a faster and heavier penalty than a fine.

questions.question: What is the most common weakness in proposals?
options: Describing activities rather than measurable results
questions.explanation: Funders assess the change produced, not the number of activities delivered.

questions.question: How are most interview questions best answered?
options: With general statements about your qualities
With specific examples including a measurable result
By describing the course you took
questions.explanation: Concrete examples with results are checkable evidence, unlike general claims.

questions.question: Why are traditional fixed planting calendars becoming less reliable?
options: Because rainfall has become less predictable
Because calendars are no longer printed
Because soil no longer holds water
questions.explanation: Increasing climate variability widens the window in which rains begin, so a fixed date no longer matches conditions.

questions.question: Which soil property cannot be changed by management?
questions.explanation: Texture is the fixed proportion of sand, silt and clay; the others can all be modified.

questions.question: When does an innovation actually count as adopted?
questions.explanation: Innovation in practice is measured by adoption, not by invention or publication.

questions.question: Roughly what proportion of applied water reaches the crop under drip irrigation?
questions.explanation: Drip places water at the root with little evaporation or runoff, exceeding 90 percent efficiency.

questions.question: Why is yield per hectare an incomplete measure of productivity?
options: It only answers how well land is used
It cannot be compared over time
questions.explanation: Land is only one input, and often not the scarce one, so it cannot represent overall productivity.

questions.question: What determines whether variable rate application pays?
options: Field variation, input cost, and mapping accuracy
The size of the farm only
questions.explanation: Without real variation, an expensive input, and a usable map, the practice returns little.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of sensor-linked irrigation over a timer?
options: It knows conditions, so it does not irrigate during rain
questions.explanation: Responding to actual soil and weather conditions is where nearly all the water saving comes from.

questions.question: What does a vegetation index show?
options: Difference in vegetation vigour, not its cause
questions.explanation: Indices reveal where vigour differs; determining why requires inspection.

questions.question: Which chart shows the relationship between two measurements?
questions.explanation: Plotting one variable against the other reveals whether and how they relate.

questions.question: What is the central output of a financial plan?
questions.explanation: Monthly cash flow reveals the timing gaps that annual totals conceal.

questions.question: Why do repeat customers matter more than new ones?
options: Winning a new customer costs considerably more than keeping an existing one
questions.explanation: An established buyer needs no convincing, sampling or renegotiation.

questions.question: What two things does processing achieve?
options: Extends shelf life and captures more chain value
questions.explanation: Both preservation and value capture are the reasons to process.

questions.question: What matters more than the interest rate?
options: Whether the repayment schedule matches when income arrives
questions.explanation: A mismatch forces repayment from funds the business does not yet have, causing default.

questions.question: Which tasks suit robotics best?
options: Repetitive, precisely definable tasks done many times
questions.explanation: Repetition and precise definition are what make automation feasible and worthwhile.

questions.question: What is the economic case for a cooperative?
options: Scale, which creates a negotiating position members lack individually
questions.explanation: Aggregation gives smallholders bargaining power with buyers, suppliers and lenders.

lessons.title: 🧪 Capstone Project Evaluation
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Capstone Project Evaluation

Complete this examination/review, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What should the summary of a report do?
options: Stand alone, giving findings, meaning and recommendations
questions.explanation: The summary is often all that is read, so it must convey the essentials by itself.

questions.question: What kind of service is easiest to sell?
options: A specific, bounded service with a clear deliverable
questions.explanation: A defined deliverable is easy to price, approve and evaluate.

questions.question: Why do the agricultural foundation modules come first?
options: Because the technology modules assume that knowledge
questions.explanation: Applying technology requires understanding the system it is applied to, so the foundation must come first.

questions.question: When does water stress usually do the most damage?
questions.explanation: Flowering and filling are the critical stages when yield is being set, so stress then is disproportionately costly.

questions.question: Why is comparing two different plots often misleading?
options: Because they differ in more ways than the one you changed
questions.explanation: Confounding factors such as soil depth or water access can explain the difference instead of the treatment.

questions.question: Why does removing a crop for a season reduce its pests?
options: Most pests are host-specific and starve without their host
questions.explanation: Host specificity means that removing the host breaks the pest's life cycle.

questions.question: Why must labour planning focus on peaks rather than annual totals?
options: Critical tasks must happen in narrow windows or lose their value
questions.explanation: Timeliness determines value, so a shortfall during the critical weeks cannot be made up later.

questions.question: What three things does precision irrigation require knowing?
options: Crop variety, plot size and price
Pump size, fuel cost and labour
Soil moisture, crop water use, and system delivery rate
questions.explanation: Without all three, the amount of water actually needed and delivered cannot be matched.

questions.question: What are the two highest-value uses of livestock monitoring?
options: Oestrus detection and early illness detection
questions.explanation: Both catch changes in activity before they are visible, which is where the economic value lies.

questions.question: What is the main limitation of aerial pest detection?
options: It sees damage only after harm has been done, and cannot identify the pest
questions.explanation: Canopy-level symptoms appear after the pest has already caused measurable damage.

questions.question: What are the four sources of yield difference?
options: Site, season, management and measurement error
questions.explanation: A useful analysis attributes differences among these rather than assuming one cause.

questions.question: Why are prices lowest just after harvest?
options: Because everyone sells at the same time
questions.explanation: Simultaneous supply from all producers pushes the price down.

questions.question: When is digital advertising worth doing?
options: When the result can be measured
questions.explanation: Without measurement there is no way to distinguish effective spending from waste.

questions.question: How does quality assurance differ from quality control?
options: Assurance is done by buyers; control by farmers
Assurance applies only to processed food
Assurance designs the process to prevent failures; control inspects and rejects
questions.explanation: Prevention through process design differs fundamentally from detection after the fact.

questions.question: How does index insurance determine payouts?
options: By assessing each farm's actual loss
By a measured index crossing a threshold
questions.explanation: Payment follows the index value rather than any individual assessment, which keeps costs low.

lessons.title: 🧪 Portfolio Review
lessons.html:
Module 20: Assessments & GraduationAssessment

Portfolio Review

Complete this examination/review, then review every answer explanation to strengthen your weak areas.

questions.question: What does a blockchain guarantee?
options: That the recorded data is accurate
That the record has not been altered after entry
questions.explanation: Immutability protects against later alteration, not against a false original entry.

questions.question: What is often a bigger constraint on farm income than yield?
questions.explanation: Produce that cannot reach a buyer at acceptable cost earns little regardless of how much is grown.

questions.question: What should be assumed first when cross-team work fails?
options: That the problem is structural rather than personal
questions.explanation: Unclear handovers and incompatible schedules cause most such failures.

questions.question: What does a consultant sell that a freelancer does not?
questions.explanation: Clients pay for an assessment they cannot confidently make themselves.

questions.question: What is the key question to ask about any agricultural recommendation?
options: How many people have shared it?
Under what conditions was it tested?
questions.explanation: A result only transfers to your farm if the testing conditions resemble yours, so conditions are the first question.

questions.question: Why can pest outbreaks follow spraying rather than precede it?
options: Because natural enemies are killed and recover more slowly than pests
Because spraying attracts pests from other farms
questions.explanation: Broad-spectrum sprays destroy predators and parasitoids, and pests rebound faster than the enemies that controlled them.

questions.question: Which three conditions justify automating a farm task?
options: The task is repetitive, timing matters, and labour is scarce or costly
The task is new, seasonal and outdoors
The farm is large, wealthy and modern
The task is difficult, dirty and dangerous only
questions.explanation: These three together determine whether automation returns more than it costs.

questions.question: What usually makes organic production economically viable?
options: Access to a market that pays a premium
questions.explanation: Yields typically fall and labour rises, so the premium is what makes the economics work.

questions.question: Why is controlling a hazard better than relying on care?
options: Guards protect permanently while attention lapses
questions.explanation: Engineering controls work continuously and do not depend on anyone remembering.

questions.question: What is a composite sample?
options: A sample split between two laboratories
One scoop taken from the field centre
Several sub-samples from across a zone mixed together
A sample taken at two depths
questions.explanation: Combining sub-samples makes the result represent the zone rather than one arbitrary point.

questions.question: Why must temperature and humidity be managed together?
options: They are measured by the same sensor
Closing vents to hold temperature raises humidity and disease risk
questions.explanation: The actions that control one variable directly affect the other, so they cannot be set independently.

questions.question: What prevents most drone incidents?
options: Procedures: checklists, a defined area and landing rules
questions.explanation: Almost all incidents trace to procedural lapses rather than lack of piloting ability.

questions.question: How is break-even yield calculated?
options: Total variable cost divided by price per unit
questions.explanation: It is the output needed for revenue to cover the variable costs incurred.

questions.question: What is a brand, for a farm product?
options: What a buyer expects from you before inspecting the goods
questions.explanation: It is a promise about what will be delivered, which is why consistency underpins it.

questions.question: How does content marketing differ from advertising?
options: It works slowly and compounds, rather than stopping when payment stops
questions.explanation: Published usefulness continues to attract an audience long after it is created.

Certificate Requirements

Certificate Requirements is an AgriTech concept or practice used to improve agricultural decisions, productivity, resilience, safety, or market value.

field evidence

measurements, observations, records, photographs, samples, or verified reports used to support an agricultural conclusion

agronomy

the science and practice of managing soil and crops for productive, sustainable agriculture

farm decision

a choice about production, resources, timing, risk, markets, or technology based on goals and evidence

📖 Certificate Requirements
The final check before graduation, and what happens after.

You have reached the graduation module. This lesson confirms exactly what must be complete and lets you check your own position before the final assessment.

Module 1 introduced these requirements at the start so you could work towards them. This is the point at which they are verified.

Key points

  • Lessons — every content lesson in Modules 1 to 18 completed.
  • Projects — all ten real-world AgriTech projects in Module 17.
  • Capstone — the eight stages of Module 19, with the digital farm portfolio submitted.
  • Assessments — the skill assessments, Midterm and Final Examinations, Capstone Evaluation and Portfolio Review all passed.
  • Final assessment — the Certificate of Completion assessment passed.
  • Check each one against your own record before sitting the final assessment.

Example

A learner reviewing this list finds that seven of the ten Module 17 projects are complete and that the capstone budget stage was never written up. Both are recoverable in a fortnight. Discovering it here rather than after the final assessment is the point of this lesson.

Why this matters

The certificate records that you completed defined work to a standard, which is what makes it worth something to an employer. Beyond it, the portfolio you built is the part that will actually get you interviews — keep it current, and keep adding to it as you work.

questions.question: What does traceability rest on?
questions.explanation: Grouping produce into identifiable batches is what makes tracking possible.

questions.question: Why do most grant applications fail?
questions.explanation: Applicants frequently apply for funds they were never qualified to receive.

questions.question: How should an AI tool be tested before it is trusted?
options: On cases where the correct answer is already known
questions.explanation: Local validation against known answers reveals actual accuracy under your conditions.

questions.question: What explains the yield gap between men and women farmers?
options: Differences in access to land, credit, inputs and services
questions.explanation: With equal access, yields are comparable, so the gap reflects access rather than capability.

questions.question: What is the usual error in problem solving?
options: Treating a symptom rather than finding the cause
questions.explanation: Responding to the visible symptom leaves the underlying cause in place.

questions.question: When is a certification worth pursuing?
options: When it can be completed quickly
When it is required for roles you want, grants a permission, or teaches a real gap
When it is the cheapest option
questions.explanation: These three cases produce a concrete return; general credentialing usually does not.

questions.question: What do you need in order to complete the practical work?
options: A commercial drone and a soil laboratory
A phone, a notebook and access to one working farm
At least ten hectares of your own land
questions.explanation: Every project is designed to be completed with a phone, a notebook and access to a single working farm.

questions.question: What is the difference between yield and production?
options: Yield is output per unit area; production is total output
Yield is measured in money; production in weight
questions.explanation: Yield is per hectare while production is the total, which is why production can rise as yield falls.

questions.question: Why can technically correct advice still produce no change?
options: Because it may arrive in the wrong language, at the wrong time, or from an untrusted source
questions.explanation: The channel determines whether advice is received and acted on, independently of whether it is correct.

questions.question: What does additionality mean in carbon credits?
options: Carbon must be added to the soil by machine
The carbon must be additional to what would have happened anyway
Additional farms must join each year
Extra payment is made for large farms
questions.explanation: Credits pay for sequestration that would not have occurred without the project.

questions.question: What are the four possible responses to a risk?
questions.explanation: Every risk is handled by one of these four, and accepting should be a conscious decision.

questions.question: What makes precision crop management a cycle rather than a purchase?
options: Each season's results refine the next season's zones
questions.explanation: The yield map produced at harvest becomes the input to the following season's zone definition.

questions.question: What three things must be attached to every reading?
questions.explanation: Without these a reading cannot be interpreted or compared.

questions.question: Who regulates drone operation?
questions.explanation: Drones are aircraft, so aviation authorities set the rules for their operation.

questions.question: When is it reasonable to act on weak evidence?
options: When the decision is cheap and reversible
questions.explanation: Low cost of error and easy reversal make acting and learning cheaper than waiting.
